title: Advanced Pricing Strategies

learningObjectives.text: Know and understand the following economic terms: block pricing, commodity bundling, cross-subsidies, price discrimination, peak-load pricing, two-part pricing, transfer pricing
Know and understand the three forms of price discrimination
Know how to calculate the profit-maximizing price when using two-part pricing, block pricing, commodity bundling, peak-load pricing, cross-subsidies, and transfer pricing
Be able to articulate the benefits and risks of charging different prices to different customers

keyTerms.def: Charging different prices to different consumers (or for different units) for the same good, where the price differences are not due to cost differences.
Charging each consumer the maximum they are willing to pay for each unit; the firm captures all consumer surplus.
Charging a per-unit price that depends on how many units are bought (e.g., quantity discounts); consumers self-select.
Charging different groups (with different, identifiable elasticities) different prices, e.g., student or senior discounts. Charge the higher price to the less elastic group.
A fixed fee for the right to buy plus a per-unit price. Profit-maximizing: set per-unit price = MC and the fixed fee = the consumer surplus each consumer receives at that price.
Selling identical units only in a package (block); the profit-maximizing package price equals the total value (area under demand) of the package quantity, where package quantity is where P = MC.
Selling two or more different products together for a single price; profitable when consumers' reservation prices are negatively correlated and the firm cannot price discriminate.
Charging a higher price during peak demand (when capacity is constrained and MC is high) and a lower price off-peak. Set P where MR = MC in each period.
Pricing one product below cost (or low) to boost demand for a complementary product that earns the profit (e.g., cheap printers, profitable ink).

Setting the internal price at which an upstream division sells an input to a downstream division of the same firm; to maximize overall firm profit (no external market), set the transfer price equal to the upstream division's marginal cost.

formulas.name: Block price
formulas.latex: \text{Package price} = MC\cdot Q + CS \text{ at } P=MC

traps: Third-degree: higher price to the LESS elastic group
Two-part pricing: per-unit price at MC, not at the monopoly price
Bundling only helps when reservation prices are negatively correlated
